qualification: local A05.3 reliability isolation; not A05.3 closure, performance acceptance, cross-host, G1-G5, or release qualification

candidate.acceptedBoundary: The experimental production PC machine exposed the generated IBTC and shadow-return stack while disabling both direct-source classes. Chained CALL blocks may enter generated accounting to publish shadow records, but direct patch installation remains independently disabled.
candidate.behavioralIntent: Measure the shadow-return delta over the accepted IBTC-only boundary without enabling legacy or Tier-one direct links.
candidate.productionFinding: Two runs of the exact same hashed release runner passed all seven authenticated workloads and powered off. Both exercised shadow pushes and hits plus IBTC fallback while recording zero direct-chain patches. This accepts the accounting fix and the shadow-return path as a bounded isolated reliability boundary. Total dispatcher avoidance remained effectively unchanged from IBTC-only, so production returns to the higher-avoidance Tier-one-direct boundary.

verification.focused: 39 tests in two suites passed, including explicit IBTC-only and IBTC-plus-shadow runtime boundaries plus PC machine coverage.
verification.deterministicAggregate: 1,558 tests in 179 suites passed with test parallelism disabled.

comparison.finding: Adding the shadow-return stack shifts warm return prediction from the IBTC to the shadow stack, but total generated bypasses and approximately 0.91-percent within-run dispatcher avoidance remain essentially unchanged.

retainedProductionBoundary.reason: Tier-one-only direct chaining produced approximately 36.45-percent within-run avoidance, versus approximately 0.91 percent for IBTC plus shadow returns.

disposition.reason: The shadow-specific implementation and regression are retained, but production returns to Tier-one-only direct chaining. A05.3 remains open for safe predictor combinations and a final enabled path exceeding 95-percent dispatcher avoidance.

limitations: Two passing local runs are a bounded reliability check, not cross-host qualification or proof that every intermittent failure has been eliminated.
The experiment establishes IBTC-plus-shadow behavior only; it does not establish safety when combined with either direct-source class.
The approximately 0.91-percent within-run avoidance is below the strict A05.3 performance threshold.
The raw diagnostic receipts remain in /private/tmp; this checked-in record binds their hashes and selected counters.
